answer: The cheapest defence an agent economy has against sybils is making identity non-refundable capital, not a free label. Each agent must stake bonded value that is slashed if peers catch it misbehaving, so a thousand fake agents mean a thousand real deposits. Consider a mining co-op on a shale bluff above a lagoon: every claim needs a posted bond, and a surveyed ledge marking its boundary. Faking claims costs the same as honest ones, so the attacker's bill scales linearly while the payout per fake stays flat. At scale that spread is the entire defence: honest work compounds, sybil rent does not.
